name: Certify exact published candidate
'on':
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      preserve_artifacts:
        description: Keep temporary handoffs and diagnostics for one day after completion
        type: boolean
        default: false
      tag:
        description: Exact published candidate tag
        type: string
        required: true
      inventory:
        description: Exact release.json SHA-256
        type: string
        required: true
      profile:
        description: Support policy profile
        type: choice
        options:
        - core
        - all-gui
        default: core
      graphics_archive_url:
        description: Operator-retained HTTPS host graphics archive; required for Windows GUI checks
        type: string
        default: ''
      linux_pool:
        description: Authorized runner pool
        type: choice
        options: [standard, faster]
        default: standard
      execute:
        description: Append this immutable certificate attempt to the candidate
        type: boolean
        default: false
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      preserve_artifacts:
        description: Keep temporary handoffs and diagnostics for one day after completion
        type: boolean
        default: false
      tag:
        description: Exact published candidate tag
        type: string
        required: true
      inventory:
        description: Exact release.json SHA-256
        type: string
        required: true
      profile:
        description: Support policy profile
        type: string
        default: core
      graphics_archive_url:
        description: Operator-retained HTTPS host graphics archive; required for Windows GUI checks
        type: string
        default: ''
      linux_pool:
        description: Authorized runner pool
        type: string
        default: standard
      execute:
        description: Append this immutable certificate attempt to the candidate
        type: boolean
        default: false
    outputs:
      certificate_sha256:
        description: Verified certificate sha256
        value: ${{ jobs.record.outputs.certificate_sha256 }}
      certification_run:
        description: Verified certification run
        value: ${{ jobs.record.outputs.certification_run }}
      certification_attempt:
        description: Verified certification attempt
        value: ${{ jobs.record.outputs.certification_attempt }}
      inventory_sha256:
        description: Verified inventory sha256
        value: ${{ jobs.record.outputs.inventory_sha256 }}
      eligible_for_promotion:
        description: Verified eligible for promotion
        value: ${{ jobs.record.outputs.eligible_for_promotion }}
      attached:
        description: Verified attached
        value: ${{ jobs.attach.outputs.attached }}
permissions:
  contents: read
  actions: read
jobs:
  prepare:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      control_attempt: ${{ steps.origin.outputs.attempt }}
      matrix: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.matrix }}
      max_parallel: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.max_parallel }}
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
      with:
        persist-credentials: false
    - name: Retain the original control attempt
      id: origin
      shell: python
      run: |
        import os
        from pathlib import Path
        with Path(os.environ['GITHUB_OUTPUT']).open('a', encoding='utf-8') as stream:
            stream.write('attempt=' + os.environ['GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT'] + '\n')
    - shell: python
      run: |-
        import subprocess, sys
        subprocess.run([sys.executable, '.github/scripts/lifecycle.py', 'certification-plan'], check=True)
      id: plan
    - name: Retain the frozen complete inventory and exact original asset identities
      run: python .github/scripts/lifecycle.py qualification-metadata-check
    - name: Retain bounded certification controls
      uses: ./.github/actions/ci-evidence-publish
      with:
        name: qualification-inputs-${{ github.run_attempt }}
        paths: |-
          build/candidate/release.json
          build/delivery.json
          build/candidate-remote.json
          build/check-plan.json
    permissions:
      contents: write
      actions: read
  check:
    name: Qualify ${{ matrix.id }}
    needs: prepare
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      max-parallel: ${{ fromJSON(needs.prepare.outputs.max_parallel) }}
      matrix: ${{ fromJSON(needs.prepare.outputs.matrix) }}
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    # Includes bounded shared GitHub quota waits as well as execution.
    timeout-minutes: 240
    env:
      CONTROL_ATTEMPT: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.control_attempt }}
      BATCH: ${{ matrix.id }}
      CHECK_IMAGE: ${{ matrix.image }}
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
      with:
        persist-credentials: false
    - name: Download bounded workflow evidence
      if: needs.prepare.outputs.control_attempt == github.run_attempt
      uses: ./.github/actions/ci-evidence-download
      with:
        pattern: qualification-inputs
    - name: Restore frozen metadata and only required original published assets
      shell: python
      env:
        CHECK_PAYLOADS: ${{ toJSON(matrix.payloads) }}
      run: |
        import subprocess,sys
        subprocess.run([sys.executable,'.github/scripts/lifecycle.py','fetch-published-check-inputs'],check=True)
    - name: Verify the explicitly supplied retained Windows graphics input
      if: runner.os == 'Windows' && matrix.graphics
      run: python .github/scripts/lifecycle.py graphics-input
    - if: runner.os == 'Windows'
      shell: pwsh
      run: ./tools/ci_windows.ps1
    - name: Run each frozen execution in the transport batch
      shell: python
      run: |-
        import subprocess, sys
        subprocess.run([sys.executable, '.github/scripts/lifecycle.py', 'check-batch'], check=True)
    - if: always()
      name: Retain verified evidence-${{ matrix.id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
      uses: ./.github/actions/ci-evidence-publish
      with:
        name: evidence-${{ matrix.id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
        slot: ${{ strategy.job-index }}
        paths: |-
          build/evidence/
          build/prerequisites/
    permissions:
      contents: write
      actions: read
  record:
    env:
      CONTROL_ATTEMPT: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.control_attempt }}
    if: always() && needs.prepare.result == 'success'
    needs:
    - prepare
    - check
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
      with:
        persist-credentials: false
    - name: Download bounded workflow evidence
      uses: ./.github/actions/ci-evidence-download
      with:
        pattern: '{qualification-inputs,evidence-*}'
    - name: Restore frozen controls and every batch outcome together
      shell: python
      env:
        CHECK_BATCHES: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.matrix }}
      run: |
        import subprocess,sys
        subprocess.run([sys.executable,'.github/scripts/lifecycle.py','fetch-certification-evidence'],check=True)
    - shell: python
      run: |-
        import subprocess, sys
        subprocess.run([sys.executable, '.github/scripts/lifecycle.py', 'certificate'], check=True)
      id: result
    - if: always()
      id: certificate_bundle
      name: Retain verified certificate-${{ github.run_attempt }}
      uses: ./.github/actions/ci-evidence-publish
      with:
        name: certificate-${{ github.run_attempt }}
        paths: |-
          build/candidate/release.json
          build/delivery.json
          build/candidate-remote.json
          build/check-plan.json
          build/evidence/
          build/certificate.json
          build/attachment-plan.json
          build/transport-receipts/
    permissions:
      contents: write
      actions: read
    outputs:
      certificate_artifact_id: ${{ steps.certificate_bundle.outputs.artifact-id }}
      certificate_sha256: ${{ steps.result.outputs.certificate_sha256 }}
      certification_run: ${{ steps.result.outputs.certification_run }}
      certification_attempt: ${{ steps.result.outputs.certification_attempt }}
      inventory_sha256: ${{ steps.result.outputs.inventory_sha256 }}
      eligible_for_promotion: ${{ steps.result.outputs.eligible_for_promotion }}
  attach:
    env:
      CERTIFICATE_ATTEMPT: ${{ needs.record.outputs.certification_attempt }}
      CERTIFICATE_SHA256: ${{ needs.record.outputs.certificate_sha256 }}
    if: inputs.execute && always() && needs.record.result == 'success'
    needs: record
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    environment: release-publisher
    concurrency:
      group: foundation-release-lifecycle
      cancel-in-progress: false
    permissions:
      contents: write
      actions: write
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
      with:
        persist-credentials: false
    - name: Download bounded certificate evidence
      if: needs.record.outputs.certification_attempt == github.run_attempt
      uses: ./.github/actions/ci-evidence-download
      with:
        pattern: certificate
    - shell: python
      run: |
        import subprocess,sys
        subprocess.run([sys.executable,'.github/scripts/lifecycle.py','fetch-certificate'],check=True)
    - shell: python
      run: |-
        import subprocess, sys
        subprocess.run([sys.executable, '.github/scripts/lifecycle.py', 'attach-certificate'], check=True)
      id: result
    - if: always()
      name: Retain verified certification-delivery-${{ github.run_attempt }}
      uses: ./.github/actions/ci-evidence-publish
      with:
        name: certification-delivery-${{ github.run_attempt }}
        paths: build/receipts/
    - name: Remove the certificate handoff after verified public attachment
      if: success() && !inputs.preserve_artifacts && steps.result.outputs.attached == 'true'
      uses: ./.github/actions/ci-artifact-cleanup
      continue-on-error: true
      timeout-minutes: 1
      with:
        artifact-ids: '[${{ toJSON(needs.record.outputs.certificate_artifact_id) }}]'
    outputs:
      attached: ${{ steps.result.outputs.attached }}
  verdict:
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read
    if: always()
    needs:
    - prepare
    - check
    - record
    - attach
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    env:
      RESULTS: ${{ toJSON(needs) }}
      EXECUTE: ${{ inputs.execute }}
    steps:
    - shell: python
      run: |
        import json,os
        results=json.loads(os.environ['RESULTS'])
        required=['prepare','check','record'] + (['attach'] if os.environ['EXECUTE']=='true' else [])
        if any(results[k]['result'] != 'success' for k in required): raise SystemExit('Incomplete or failed exact qualification; inspect retained evidence')

env:
  GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
  PYTHONUTF8: '1'
  PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE: '1'
  TAG: ${{ inputs.tag }}
  INVENTORY: ${{ inputs.inventory }}
  PROFILE: ${{ inputs.profile }}
  CERTIFICATION_JOBS: ${{ vars.FOUNDATION_CERTIFICATION_JOBS || '0' }}
  LINUX_POOL: ${{ inputs.linux_pool }}
  FOUNDATION_FASTER_LINUX_RUNNER: ${{ vars.FOUNDATION_FAST_LINUX_RUNNER }}
  FOUNDATION_FASTER_ARM_RUNNER: ${{ vars.FOUNDATION_FAST_ARM_RUNNER }}
  FOUNDATION_FASTER_WINDOWS_RUNNER: ${{ vars.FOUNDATION_FAST_WINDOWS_RUNNER }}
  GRAPHICS_ARCHIVE_URL: ${{ inputs.graphics_archive_url }}

name: Development feedback
on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]
permissions:
  contents: read
concurrency:
  group: feedback-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
jobs:
  focused:
    name: Focused checks (not release qualification)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          fetch-depth: 2
      - name: Select conservative feedback scope from local Git
        id: changes
        run: python3 -B tools/ci_changes.py
      - name: Require an explicit selection
        env:
          SELECTED: ${{ steps.changes.outputs.build }}
        run: test "$SELECTED" = true || test "$SELECTED" = false
      - name: Validate narrative documents
        if: steps.changes.outputs.build == 'false'
        run: python3 -B tools/check_docs.py
      - name: Prepare distribution Rust host tools
        if: steps.changes.outputs.build == 'true'
        run: sudo sh tools/ci-apt.sh install rustc cargo
      - name: Build and test inexpensive contracts
        if: steps.changes.outputs.build == 'true'
        run: PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:$PATH python3 tools/build.py test dev --core-provider rust --label fast --test-jobs 2
      - name: Explicit C++ compatibility contracts
        if: steps.changes.outputs.build == 'true'
        run: python3 tools/build.py test dev --core-provider cpp --build-dir build/cpp-compat --label core --test-jobs 2
      - name: Scope
        if: always()
        run: echo 'Focused feedback only. Full tools, platform, package and GUI qualification are separate.' >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

  workflow-syntax:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          fetch-depth: 2
      - name: Select conservative feedback scope from local Git
        id: changes
        run: python3 -B tools/ci_changes.py
      - name: Require an explicit selection
        env:
          SELECTED: ${{ steps.changes.outputs.workflow_lint }}
        run: test "$SELECTED" = true || test "$SELECTED" = false
      - name: Validate workflows with installed or exact retained validator
        if: steps.changes.outputs.workflow_lint == 'true'
        run: python3 tools/ci_plan.py workflow-lint --retained-url "$RETAINED_URL" --executable "$VALIDATOR" --output build/workflow-lint
        env:
          RETAINED_URL: ${{ vars.FOUNDATION_ACTIONLINT_URL }}
          VALIDATOR: ${{ vars.FOUNDATION_ACTIONLINT_EXECUTABLE }}

  shared-gui:
    name: Shared GUI contracts and generic hosts
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          fetch-depth: 2
      - name: Select conservative feedback scope from local Git
        id: changes
        run: python3 -B tools/ci_changes.py
      - name: Require an explicit selection
        env:
          SELECTED: ${{ steps.changes.outputs.gui }}
        run: test "$SELECTED" = true || test "$SELECTED" = false
      - name: Prepare distribution Rust host tools
        if: steps.changes.outputs.gui == 'true'
        run: sudo sh tools/ci-apt.sh install rustc cargo
      - name: Compile shared application once and check generic hosts
        if: steps.changes.outputs.gui == 'true'
        run: PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:$PATH python3 -B tools/build.py test dev --core-provider rust --gui --gui-backends terminal,framebuffer,hosted-web --host-tests --label gui --test-jobs 2

  changed-tools:
    name: Affected complete infrastructure suites
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          fetch-depth: 2
      - name: Select conservative feedback scope from local Git
        id: changes
        run: python3 -B tools/ci_changes.py
      - name: Require an explicit selection
        env:
          SELECTED: ${{ steps.changes.outputs.tools }}
        run: test "$SELECTED" = true || test "$SELECTED" = false
      - name: Run affected whole tooling suites with strict case outcomes
        if: steps.changes.outputs.tools == 'true'
        run: python3 -B tools/ci_changes.py --run-tool-suites --tool-jobs 2 --tool-output build/changed-tools
      - name: Preserve complete tooling outcome receipts
        if: always() && steps.changes.outputs.tools == 'true'
        uses: ./.github/actions/ci-evidence-publish
        with:
          name: evidence-batch-feedback-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          slot: 0
          paths: build/changed-tools/*.json

name: Signed immutable package channel
'on':

    inputs:
      request:
        description: Complete distribution request JSON; see docs/distribution-release.md
        type: string
        required: true
      previous:
        description: Optional prior exact channel JSON for native upgrade qualification
        type: string
        default: ''
      execute:
        description: Sign and publish the separately certified package channel
        type: boolean
        default: false
permissions:
  contents: read
  actions: read
concurrency:
  group: foundation-distribution-${{ fromJSON(inputs.request).target }}
  cancel-in-progress: false
env:
  PYTHONUTF8: '1'
  PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE: '1'
  GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
jobs:
  plan:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      tag: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.tag }}
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      with:
        persist-credentials: false
    - id: plan
      name: Validate exact request without signing or remote mutation
      shell: python
      env:
        REQUEST: ${{ inputs.request }}
      run: |
        import json, os, sys
        from pathlib import Path
        sys.path.insert(0, 'tools')
        import distribution_release as channel
        raw = os.environ['REQUEST']
        request = channel.workflow_request(raw)
        if request.get('repository') != os.environ['GITHUB_REPOSITORY'] or request.get('packager_commit') != os.environ['GITHUB_SHA']:
            raise ValueError('request must name this repository and exact packaging revision')
        result = channel.plan(request)
        with Path(os.environ['GITHUB_OUTPUT']).open('a') as stream:
            stream.write('tag=' + result['tag'] + '\n')
        with Path(os.environ['GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY']).open('a') as stream:
            stream.write('Planned independent non-Latest package channel:\n```json\n' + json.dumps(result, indent=2) + '\n```\n')
  publish:
    outputs:
      channel: ${{ steps.publish.outputs.channel }}
    if: ${{ inputs.execute }}
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 90
    environment: release-publisher
    permissions:
      contents: write
      actions: read
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      with:
        persist-credentials: false
    - name: Install ordinary package and signing tools
      run: sudo sh tools/ci-apt.sh install dpkg-dev gnupg gpgv binutils
    - name: Verify existing certificate, sign, read back and publish independent channel
      id: publish
      shell: python
      env:
        REQUEST: ${{ inputs.request }}
        SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.DISTRIBUTION_SIGNING_KEY }}
        TRUSTED_FINGERPRINT: ${{ vars.DISTRIBUTION_SIGNING_FINGERPRINT }}
      run: |
        import json, os, subprocess, sys, tempfile
        from pathlib import Path
        sys.path.insert(0, 'tools')
        import distribution_release as channel
        raw = os.environ['REQUEST']
        request = channel.workflow_request(raw)
        if request['repository'] != os.environ['GITHUB_REPOSITORY'] or request['packager_commit'] != os.environ['GITHUB_SHA']:
            raise ValueError('request differs from selected checkout')
        if request['trusted_fingerprint'] != os.environ['TRUSTED_FINGERPRINT']:
            raise ValueError('request fingerprint differs from protected independent trust setting')
        # Remove key material from the environment before creating subprocesses.
        private = os.environ.pop('SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY')
        if not private or len(private.encode()) > 1024 * 1024:
            raise ValueError('bounded protected signing key required')
        output = Path('build/distribution')
        output.parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        channel.archive.write_json(output.parent / 'distribution-request.json', request)
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='foundation-private-key-', dir=os.environ['RUNNER_TEMP']) as temporary:
            key = Path(temporary) / 'private.asc'
            key.write_text(private); key.chmod(0o600)
            del private
            subprocess.run([sys.executable, '-B', 'tools/distribution_release.py', 'prepare',
                '--request', str(output.parent / 'distribution-request.json'), '--output', str(output),
                '--signing-key', str(key)], check=True, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL)
        result = channel.publish(output, Path('docs/release-policy.json'), request['trusted_fingerprint'], execute=True)
        channel.archive.write_json(output.parent / 'distribution-publication.json', result)
        selected = dict(tag=result['tag'], manifest_sha256=result['manifest_sha256'], target=request['target'])
        with Path(os.environ['GITHUB_OUTPUT']).open('a') as stream:
            stream.write('channel=' + json.dumps(selected) + '\n')
        with Path(os.environ['GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY']).open('a') as stream:
            stream.write('Verified signed non-Latest package channel:\n```json\n' + json.dumps(result, indent=2) + '\n```\n')
    - name: Retain signed controls and receipt; preserve complete prepared bytes on failure
      if: ${{ always() && hashFiles('build/distribution/distribution.json') != '' }}
      run: python .github/scripts/lifecycle.py bundle-store
      env:
        BUNDLE_NAME: distribution-${{ github.run_attempt }}
        BUNDLE_PATHS: |
          ${{ steps.publish.outcome != 'success' && 'build/distribution/' || 'build/distribution/distribution.json' }}
          ${{ steps.publish.outcome == 'success' && 'build/distribution/distribution.json.sig' || '' }}
          ${{ steps.publish.outcome == 'success' && 'build/distribution/archive-keyring.gpg' || '' }}
          build/distribution-request.json
          build/distribution-publication.json

  qualify:
    if: ${{ inputs.execute }}
    needs: publish
    permissions:
      contents: write
      actions: read
    uses: ./.github/workflows/distro-check.yml
    with:
      channel: ${{ needs.publish.outputs.channel }}
      previous: ${{ inputs.previous }}
      distro: all
      accept: true

name: Native signed package install and update
'on':
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      channel:
        description: Exact JSON containing tag, manifest_sha256 and target
        type: string
        required: true
      previous:
        description: Optional older exact channel JSON for an actual version upgrade
        type: string
        default: ''
      distro:
        description: Native frontend to diagnose; full acceptance requires all
        type: choice
        options: [all, apt, arch, gentoo]
        default: all
      accept:
        description: Mark this immutable channel qualified after every required native check
        type: boolean
        default: false
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      channel:
        type: string
        required: true
      previous:
        type: string
        default: ''
      distro:
        type: string
        default: all
      accept:
        type: boolean
        default: false
permissions:
  contents: read
  actions: read
env:
  GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
  PYTHONUTF8: '1'
  PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE: '1'
  CHANNEL: ${{ inputs.channel }}
  PREVIOUS: ${{ inputs.previous }}
  DISTRO: ${{ inputs.distro || 'all' }}
  ACCEPT_CHANNEL: ${{ inputs.accept }}
  TRUSTED_FINGERPRINT: ${{ vars.DISTRIBUTION_SIGNING_FINGERPRINT }}
jobs:
  plan:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      matrix: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.matrix }}
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
      with:
        persist-credentials: false
    - id: plan
      shell: python
      run: |
        import json, os, sys
        from pathlib import Path
        sys.path.insert(0, 'tools')
        import distro_check
        value = distro_check.selection(os.environ['CHANNEL'])
        if os.environ['PREVIOUS']:
            previous = distro_check.selection(os.environ['PREVIOUS'])
            if previous['target'] != value['target']:
                raise ValueError('upgrade target differs')
        with Path(os.environ['GITHUB_OUTPUT']).open('a') as stream:
            stream.write('matrix=' + json.dumps(distro_check.matrix(value['target'], os.environ['DISTRO'], accept=os.environ['ACCEPT_CHANNEL'] == 'true')) + '\n')
  install:
    needs: plan
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix: ${{ fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.matrix) }}
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    # Upgrades preserve two complete native installation rounds; SDK recovery is separate.
    timeout-minutes: ${{ matrix.kind == 'gentoo' && inputs.previous != '' && 180 || 90 }}
    permissions:
      contents: write
      actions: read
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
      with:
        persist-credentials: false
    - name: Fetch signed native channel bytes and reconcile the complete release inventory
      shell: python
      run: |
        import os, sys
        from pathlib import Path
        sys.path.insert(0, 'tools')
        import distro_check as check
        for name, raw in [('current', os.environ['CHANNEL']), ('previous', os.environ['PREVIOUS'])]:
            if not raw: continue
            item = check.selection(raw)
            value = check.release.fetch(os.environ['GITHUB_REPOSITORY'], item['tag'], item['manifest_sha256'],
                Path('build/channels')/name, Path('docs/release-policy.json'), os.environ['TRUSTED_FINGERPRINT'], native_only=True,
                reuse=Path('build/channels/current') if name == 'previous' else None)
            if value['request']['target'] != item['target']:
                raise ValueError('fetched target differs')
    - name: Install the job-owned external display service from the runner distribution
      run: |
        sudo apt-get update
        sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends xvfb xauth x11-utils
    - name: Run native package frontend in an isolated disposable system
      shell: python
      env:
        CHECK_ID: ${{ matrix.id }}
        CHECK_IMAGE: ${{ matrix.image }}
        CHECK_KIND: ${{ matrix.kind }}
      run: |
        import os, sys
        from pathlib import Path
        sys.path.insert(0, 'tools')
        import distro_check
        distro_check.container(Path.cwd(), os.environ['CHECK_ID'], os.environ)
    - if: always()
      name: Retain complete native client evidence without Actions artifact storage
      run: python .github/scripts/lifecycle.py bundle-store
      env:
        BUNDLE_NAME: distro-${{ matrix.id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
        BUNDLE_PATHS: build/distro-evidence/
  accept:
    if: ${{ inputs.accept }}
    needs: [plan, install]
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    environment: release-publisher
    permissions:
      contents: write
      actions: read
    concurrency:
      group: foundation-release-lifecycle
      cancel-in-progress: false
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
      with:
        persist-credentials: false
    - name: Verify all native receipts and mark channel eligible for tracked updates
      shell: python
      run: |
        import os, sys
        from pathlib import Path
        sys.path.insert(0, 'tools')
        import distro_check as check
        import ci_plan
        request = check.selection(os.environ['CHANNEL'])
        records = []
        workflow = os.environ['GITHUB_WORKFLOW_REF'].split('/.github/workflows/',1)[1].split('@',1)[0]
        for row in check.matrix(request['target'])['include']:
            root = Path('build/distro-results')/row['id']
            ci_plan.restore_run_bundle(os.environ['GITHUB_REPOSITORY'], int(os.environ['GITHUB_RUN_ID']),
                int(os.environ['GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT']), os.environ['GITHUB_SHA'], workflow,
                'distro-'+row['id']+'-'+os.environ['GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT'], root)
            records.append(check.release.archive.read_json(root/'native/result.json'))
        check.accept(request, records, os.environ, Path('build/accepted-channel'))

name: Explicit retained GUI input maintenance
'on':

        description: Publish verified redistributable complete group into base

permissions:

  publish:

name: Host contract diagnostics
run-name: Host ${{ inputs.target }} / Python ${{ inputs.interpreter }} / ${{ inputs.suite }} / ${{ inputs.repetitions }} repetitions
'on':
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      target:
        description: Native runner target
        type: choice
        default: windows-x86_64
        options: [windows-x86_64, linux-x86_64, linux-aarch64]
      suite:
        description: Complete registered suite or opt-in Windows host probes
        type: choice
        default: process_tree
        options: [process_tree, windows_graphics, ci_plan, github_release, ci_transport, windows_hosts, agent_board, test_plan, ci_retry, package_wasm, import_wasm]
      interpreter:
        description: Already installed Python; explicit versions require the runner cache
        type: choice
        default: runner-default
        options: [runner-default, '3.12', '3.14']
      repetitions:
        description: Keep every repetition; any failure fails the diagnostic
        type: choice
        default: '1'
        options: ['1', '5', '20']
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  diagnose:
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.target == 'windows-x86_64' && 'windows-2022' || inputs.target == 'linux-aarch64' && 'ubuntu-24.04-arm' || 'ubuntu-24.04' }}
    # Execution is capped at 50 minutes; leave bounded headroom for evidence transport.
    timeout-minutes: 90
    permissions:
      contents: write
      actions: read
    env:
      PYTHONUTF8: '1'
      PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE: '1'
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
      with:
        persist-credentials: false
        ref: ${{ github.sha }}
    - if: inputs.target == 'windows-x86_64' && contains(fromJSON('["windows_hosts", "test_plan", "ci_retry", "package_wasm", "import_wasm"]'), inputs.suite)
      name: Select the installed native compiler for host probes
      shell: pwsh
      run: ./tools/ci_windows.ps1 -Output build/host-contracts-toolchain.json
    - name: Run complete repetitions under the selected installed interpreter
      shell: python
      env:
        DIAGNOSTIC_TARGET: ${{ inputs.target }}
        DIAGNOSTIC_SUITE: ${{ inputs.suite }}
        DIAGNOSTIC_INTERPRETER: ${{ inputs.interpreter }}
        DIAGNOSTIC_REPETITIONS: ${{ inputs.repetitions }}
      run: |
        import os, subprocess, sys
        subprocess.run([sys.executable, '-B', 'tools/host_contracts.py',
            '--target', os.environ['DIAGNOSTIC_TARGET'],
            '--suite', os.environ['DIAGNOSTIC_SUITE'],
            '--interpreter', os.environ['DIAGNOSTIC_INTERPRETER'],
            '--repetitions', os.environ['DIAGNOSTIC_REPETITIONS'],
            '--output', 'build/host-contracts'], check=True)
    - if: always()
      name: Retain diagnostic inventories and logs without Actions artifact storage
      shell: python
      env:
        GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        BUNDLE_NAME: host-contracts-${{ github.run_attempt }}
      run: |
        import os, subprocess, sys
        sys.path.insert(0, 'tools')
        import host_contracts
        os.environ['BUNDLE_PATHS'] = host_contracts.retained_paths('build/host-contracts')
        subprocess.run([sys.executable, '-B', '.github/scripts/lifecycle.py', 'bundle-store'], check=True)

name: Explicit opaque legacy artifact preservation
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      artifacts:
        description: Exact JSON list of artifact_id, sha256, run_id, source_commit, name and size
        type: string
        required: true
permissions:
  contents: read
  actions: read
jobs:
  preserve:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 180
    permissions:
      contents: write
      actions: read
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
      PYTHONUTF8: '1'
      PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE: '1'
      LEGACY_ARTIFACTS: ${{ inputs.artifacts }}
    outputs:
      pointer: ${{ steps.preserve.outputs.pointer }}
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
      with:
        persist-credentials: false
    - id: preserve
      name: Verify exact original bytes and retain private draft bundles
      run: python3 -B tools/legacy_artifacts.py --output build/legacy-preservation
    - name: Report partial-preservation pointers without claiming completion
      if: failure()
      shell: python
      run: |
        import json, os
        from pathlib import Path
        with open(os.environ['GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY'],'a',encoding='utf-8') as out:
          out.write('Preservation incomplete. Existing verified per-archive bundles remain recoverable; nothing was deleted.\n')
          for path in sorted(Path('build/legacy-preservation').glob('artifact-*.json')):
            value=json.loads(path.read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
            out.write('Completed pointer: `'+json.dumps(value['pointer'],sort_keys=True)+'`\n')

name: Explicit native GUI qualification
'on':
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      core_provider:
        description: Application provider; cpp explicitly selects legacy compatibility
        type: choice
        options: [rust, cpp]
        default: rust
      target:
        description: Native execution host
        type: choice
        options:
        - windows-x86_64
        - linux-x86_64
        - linux-aarch64
        default: windows-x86_64
      recipe:
        description: Exact complete GUI-capable dependency recipe already in base
        type: string
        required: true
      graphics_archive_url:
        description: Operator-retained HTTPS host graphics archive; required for Windows
        type: string
        default: ''
      gui_input:
        description: Optional exact existing base or retained GUI selector JSON; empty uses verified checkout inputs
        type: string
        default: ''
      development:
        description: Qualify ordinary build dev and test dev without portable mode (Linux only)
        type: boolean
        default: false
      linux_pool:
        description: Standard or explicitly configured faster native runners
        type: choice
        options: [standard, faster]
        default: standard

permissions:

  actions: read

  FOUNDATION_FASTER_LINUX_RUNNER: ${{ vars.FOUNDATION_FAST_LINUX_RUNNER }}
  FOUNDATION_FASTER_ARM_RUNNER: ${{ vars.FOUNDATION_FAST_ARM_RUNNER }}
  FOUNDATION_FASTER_WINDOWS_RUNNER: ${{ vars.FOUNDATION_FAST_WINDOWS_RUNNER }}

  GRAPHICS_ARCHIVE_URL: ${{ inputs.graphics_archive_url }}

jobs:
  plan:
    name: Validate and freeze the selected native runner
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      runner: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.runner }}
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1

    - id: plan

  qualify:

    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
      with:
        persist-credentials: false
    - name: Verify the explicitly supplied retained Windows graphics input
      if: runner.os == 'Windows'

    - if: runner.os == 'Linux'

      run: |
        import subprocess, sys
        subprocess.run([sys.executable, '.github/scripts/container_job.py', 'native-gui-check'], check=True)
    - if: always()
      name: Retain verified native-gui-evidence-${{ inputs.target }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
      run: python .github/scripts/lifecycle.py bundle-store
      env:
        BUNDLE_NAME: native-gui-evidence-${{ inputs.target }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
        BUNDLE_PATHS: |-
          ${{ job.status == 'failure' && 'build/receipts/failure.json' || '' }}
          build/native-gui/qualification.json
          build/native-gui/source.junit.xml
          build/native-gui/build/Testing/Temporary/
          build/native-gui/build/test-reports/
          build/native-gui/graphics.json
          build/native-gui/graphics-probe.json
          build/native-gui/graphics-test.log
          build/native-gui/graphics-compile.log
          build/native-gui/build/gui/visual-evidence/**/*.json
          build/native-gui/build/gui/visual-evidence/**/*.png
          build/native-gui/build/gui/visual-evidence/**/*.ppm
          build/native-gui/build/gui/visual-evidence/**/*.log
          build/host-graphics/acquisition.json

name: Focused Rev module diagnostic
run-name: Rev modules / ${{ inputs.target }}
'on':
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      target:
        description: Native runner; Linux requires the selected compiler already installed
        type: choice
        default: windows-x86_64
        options: [windows-x86_64, linux-x86_64, linux-aarch64]
      linux_compiler:
        description: Already installed Linux module compiler; unavailable tools fail without acquisition
        type: choice
        default: clang++-19
        options: [clang++-19, g++-15]
      gui_input:
        description: Exact existing retained GUI selector JSON; no source or SDK rebuild
        type: string
        required: true
      jobs:
        description: Compile parallelism within this small module graph
        type: choice
        default: auto
        options: [auto, '2', '4', '8']
permissions:
  contents: read
  actions: read
jobs:
  diagnose:
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.target == 'windows-x86_64' && 'windows-2022' || inputs.target == 'linux-aarch64' && 'ubuntu-24.04-arm' || 'ubuntu-24.04' }}
    # Each owned phase is capped at ten minutes; leave evidence-retention headroom.
    timeout-minutes: 45
    permissions:
      contents: write
      actions: read
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
      PYTHONUTF8: '1'
      PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE: '1'
      GUI_INPUT: ${{ inputs.gui_input }}
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
      with:
        persist-credentials: false
        ref: ${{ github.sha }}
    - name: Restore the exact existing retained GUI group
      run: python .github/scripts/lifecycle.py gui-input
    - if: inputs.target == 'windows-x86_64'
      name: Select the installed native MSVC toolchain
      shell: pwsh
      run: ./tools/ci_windows.ps1 -Output build/rev-probe-toolchain.json
    - id: probe
      name: Compile four production modules and run both style regressions
      shell: python
      env:
        PROBE_TARGET: ${{ inputs.target }}
        PROBE_COMPILER: ${{ inputs.linux_compiler }}
        PROBE_JOBS: ${{ inputs.jobs }}
      run: |
        import os, platform, subprocess, sys
        target = os.environ['PROBE_TARGET']
        machine = platform.machine().lower()
        expected = {'windows-x86_64': ('Windows', ('amd64', 'x86_64')),
                    'linux-x86_64': ('Linux', ('x86_64', 'amd64')),
                    'linux-aarch64': ('Linux', ('aarch64', 'arm64'))}[target]
        if platform.system() != expected[0] or machine not in expected[1]:
            raise RuntimeError('Selected diagnostic target differs from the native runner')
        compiler = 'cl.exe' if target == 'windows-x86_64' else os.environ['PROBE_COMPILER']
        subprocess.run([sys.executable, '-B', 'tools/rev_probe.py',
            '--gui-input-group', 'build/gui-group', '--compiler', compiler,
            '--jobs', os.environ['PROBE_JOBS'], '--output', 'build/rev-probe'], check=True)
    - if: always() && hashFiles('build/rev-probe/result.json') != ''
      name: Retain joined diagnostic evidence using the existing draft bundle transport
      shell: python
      env:
        BUNDLE_NAME: rev-probe-${{ inputs.target }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}-diagnostics
      run: |
        import os, subprocess, sys
        sys.path.insert(0, 'tools')
        import rev_probe
        os.environ['BUNDLE_PATHS'] = rev_probe.retained_paths('build/rev-probe')
        subprocess.run([sys.executable, '-B', '.github/scripts/lifecycle.py', 'bundle-store'], check=True)

    - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1

  verdict:
    if: always()
    needs: [plan, platform]
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04

      shell: python
      env:
        PLAN_RESULT: ${{ needs.plan.result }}
        PLATFORM_RESULT: ${{ needs.platform.result }}
      run: |
        import os
        if any(os.environ[name] != 'success' for name in ('PLAN_RESULT', 'PLATFORM_RESULT')):
            raise SystemExit('Rust qualification is incomplete or failed')

    - name: Build from existing SDKs and capture seven fresh actual surfaces

          '--rust-source', os.environ['FOUNDATION_PROVIDER_SOURCE']]

        if os.environ['FOUNDATION_NATIVE_PROVIDER_RECIPE']: command += ['--native-rust-recipe', os.environ['FOUNDATION_NATIVE_PROVIDER_RECIPE']]

        allowed = {'linux-x86_64', 'linux-aarch64', 'windows-x86_64', 'browser-wasm32'}

# Development requirements

Read [the documentation index](docs/README.md), then the pages relevant to the
change. Build through [the supported entry point](docs/building.md). Keep public
interfaces, compatibility promises and tests consistent with the implementation.
User instructions and the harness's governing rules remain authoritative.

## Parallel subagents

For substantial tasks, identify useful independent workstreams and delegate them
concurrently. Use up to 24 concurrently open spawned subagents, excluding the
primary agent, when the runtime permits and there is enough independent work.
Parallelize investigation, implementation, focused validation, documentation and
review as useful; avoid serializing independent work merely to conserve slots.
Partition edits by non-overlapping files/components and coordinate shared resources
and invariants under the project's applicable coordination requirements. The
primary agent integrates results, resolves conflicts and performs final validation.

Default subagents to `gpt-6.1-sol` with `ultra` reasoning effort, as configured in
`.codex/config.toml`. Never configure a lower model or effort as the default, or
automatically reduce below these settings to save time or tokens. A stronger
parent's settings may be preserved when appropriate. If the user explicitly
selects a lower model or effort in the desktop GUI, honor that choice with an
explicit spawn override for the selected setting; it does not change the project
defaults. If the GUI selection or model support is uncertain, do not silently
substitute a lower setting. Apply this policy to nested subagents as well.

## Development checks and manual qualification

During implementation, run inexpensive, meaningful checks that discriminate the
change and resolve immediate uncertainties. An inexpensive complete local suite
may be appropriate. By default, defer costly full regressions, broad platform or
backend matrices and complete release certification to tracked
[pending qualification](.agent-pending/README.md).

Normally start extensive final qualification only when **both implementation has
stabilized and the user explicitly requests extensive validation or a release
operation requiring it**. Stability alone is not authorization. Explicit requests
for expensive diagnostics or exploration may precede stabilization. Generic
requests to implement, fix, review, commit, merge or push do not authorize extensive
qualification; a request for a qualified binary release does. Asking for the usual
GitHub Actions binary-build and certification workflows to pass authorizes the
applicable complete workflow, even if it takes an hour or more, without separate
approval for its ordinary steps. For an unauthorized expensive diagnostic, explain
the uncertainty, why cheaper checks cannot resolve it and expected cost before
requesting execution.

Inspect relevant pending records at task start, substantive resume or scope change;
reuse reviewed information unless relevant state may have changed. At implementation
handoff, identify what passed, what remains unverified and the next manual command
or request. Clearly distinguish unfinished implementation, known failures and
implemented work awaiting extensive qualification. Unexecuted, skipped, queued or
cancelled checks are never passes. Follow the linked pending-record guide rather
than creating obligations for every available test.

Once authorized, complete the applicable workflow without repeated permission
requests. Batch independent work, reuse applicable verified results with their
original identities, avoid duplicate launches and supervise running jobs with
appropriately spaced status checks. Required gates still precede binary-release
publication and package-channel promotion; pending gates mean pending publication.
Ordinary source commits and pushes do not require complete release qualification.

## Simultaneous sessions

A supervisor may use lightweight coordination with reasonable current evidence
that it controls the writers affecting the relevant files/resources and no
independent work conflicts. It may coordinate its subagents directly and consolidate
bookkeeping. Use the [shared protocol](docs/agent-coordination.md) when independent
agents, shared resources, unresolved ownership or uncertainty require it; reassess
when circumstances change. This discretion qualifies procedural requirements in
the coordination references, but never permits overwriting another worker's changes
or ignoring known ownership. Passive read-only tools need no session.

Keep temporary coordination and generated evidence in `.agent-work/` as appropriate.
Git-ignored means excluded from Git tracking, not exempt from consultation: consult
records according to the chosen coordination mode and known ownership/handoff
dependencies.

When using the shared protocol, give each independent writer this file, that guide,
the absolute checkout and agreed absolute board path. The following requirements
apply in that mode, across chats, harnesses and writing subagents:

- Use the ignored `.agent-work/` directory for current ownership, temporary notes
  and per-session artifacts. One independent writer owns each session identity.
  Use the checked helper; do not implement ad hoc lock/unlock shell sequences.
- Use `tools/agent_session.py` for record registration, review and checked commit,
  `tools/check_agent_record.py` for bounded complete discovery, and
  `tools/agent_publish.py` for complete immutable messages. Use
  `tools/agent_edit.py` for supported existing-source replacements; otherwise use
  a qualified adapter with equivalent guarantees or isolate writes. Read the
  [exact operation recipes](docs/agent-recipes.md), including failure ordering.
  These write helpers require qualified POSIX filesystem primitives. Unsupported
  systems must fail closed; a native adapter needs equivalent tests.
- An existing `state.json` board remains on `tools/agent_board.py` until the
  [explicit migration](docs/agent-recipes.md#transition-an-existing-json-board)
  completes. Never mix protocols, initialize a second board to avoid a conflict,
  or migrate while any session or output writer is active. New boards use the
  complete record protocol directly.
- Discover complete claims, relevant releases and your inbox before acquisition.
  Bounded output must not hide owners or truncate a claim list. Unknown, corrupt
  or inaccessible data blocks affected shared writes; it never means free scope.
- Claim each file, directory and resource before writing, including unique notes,
  logs, build outputs and temporary directories. One writer per file. Claim both
  sides of a rename. Protect common Git state and shared build trees explicitly.
- Keep the registry mutex brief. File/resource claims persist after that mutex
  closes. A message, old timestamp, missing PID or empty lock never grants scope.
  Handoffs require an explicit release, fresh acquisition and acknowledgment.
- After a rejected or uncertain operation, stop its dependent saves, notices and
  launches. Inspect authoritative saved state before retrying uncertain results.
  Preserve foreign edits, staged work, processes, notes and uncommitted changes.
- Recheck input bytes and shared interface assumptions before applying an edit.
  Freeze physical identity/version and exact bytes when reviewing. Revalidate
  complete claims and scope-relevant predecessor releases at commit; an unchanged
  source hash cannot erase an intervening owner. Page discovery with its returned
  snapshot token; never combine pages from different snapshots.
  Disjoint files can change the same invariant. Stabilize inputs during tests or
  use an isolated copy containing the intended uncommitted changes.
- Record launch intent before long commands, actual yielded handles when known,
  and completion at the next checkpoint. Finish children, open output streams,
  queued saves and cleanup writers before release. Parent exit alone is not proof.
- Replace current progress, jobs, blockers and next action together; record actual
  progress/inbox event times separately from publication time. Release a finished
  shared file before unrelated reporting. Use a new ID after closure or recovery.
- Keep useful unresolved findings in owned notes: evidence, environment, source
  and access date, confidence, failed attempts, next probe and removal conditions.
  Promote verified durable knowledge into tracked documentation/tests.
- Follow [lifecycle and recovery](docs/agent-lifecycle.md) for overdue ownership,
  interrupted jobs and eligible 30-day cleanup. Never automatically steal claims.
- Coordination is cooperative. For participants that may bypass it, enforce
  private checkout/output access or read-only access through the harness or OS.
  A separate directory, stronger model, clean merge or passing tests does not
  establish exclusion before writes. Qualified participants integrate shared work.

Coordination adds no research quota, approval step, extra reports or limitation on
normal browsing, delegation and tools. Continue independent useful work when one
scope is contested. Bind every filesystem tool and subprocess to its intended
absolute checkout; another tool's current directory does not carry over.

## Implementation integrity

Use [testing stages](docs/testing.md) under the manual-qualification policy above.
Documentation changes need proportionate checks. Do not repeatedly run expensive
full suites while diagnosing one fault, weaken assertions or remove cases to
shorten iteration time.

Reuse evidence only for identical relevant source, configuration, dependencies
and environment. Name omitted coverage and its reason. Setup failure before test
assertions is zero executed assertions. Repair verified prerequisites, then rerun
the blocked scope. Separate observations from hypotheses and use a discriminating
probe before repeating a failed workaround. Preserve concise failure evidence.

Parallelize independent compilation and tests within CPU/memory limits. Use
per-session build directories and logs. A focused `devfast` configuration and an
explicitly selected faster CI runner are valid development tools when available;
restore required normal coverage before qualified binary delivery. Wait for final
results of authorized checks and inspect internal skips.

Keep application behavior and feature layout on the insulated side of the GUI
boundary. Backend adapters implement generic capabilities. Extend shared contracts
and shared tests when a new feature needs a capability; do not duplicate feature
logic across backend-specific code. Preserve the stated build and binary support
baselines, dependency provenance, SDK consumer checks and release evidence.

Before finishing, inspect the actual diff, verify observable consumer behavior,
update the relevant documentation and record exact validation with material limits.
Never stage unrelated work or publish external changes without task authorization.

## Release preferences and trust

Strongly prefer GitHub-hosted Actions for release builds and publication. Local
release builds and publication remain permitted but strongly discouraged. Hosted
publication typically avoids slow workstation transfers. Based on the maintainer's
longstanding runner observations, the project places greater trust in provider-managed
build infrastructure and its Intel TXT, AMD SEV and/or other applicable integrity
protections. Accept this project trust assumption during routine work without
repeated hardware investigations or new attestation requirements; self-hosted
Actions runners do not establish the same environment.

Preserve qualification and provenance requirements on either route, recording build
origin separately from upload location. Prefer authenticated retained CI artifacts
when their identities and qualification remain applicable, and verified retained
base-release SDKs matching the required target, profile and toolchain constraints.
Add no approval ceremony beyond the manual-qualification trigger, task authorization
and existing applicable release controls. Optional future improvements are listed
in [FURTHER-agents.txt](FURTHER-agents.txt).

function(foundation_options target)
  foundation_sdk_runtime(${target})
  if(EMSCRIPTEN)
    target_compile_options(${target} PRIVATE -fexceptions)
    target_link_options(${target} PRIVATE -fexceptions -sASSERTIONS=1)
  endif()
  if(MSVC)
    target_compile_options(${target} PRIVATE /W4 /permissive- /utf-8)
  else()
    target_compile_options(${target} PRIVATE -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic)
  endif()
  if(FOUNDATION_PORTABLE AND NOT MSVC AND NOT EMSCRIPTEN)
    if(CMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR MATCHES "^(x86_64|AMD64|amd64)$")
      target_compile_options(${target} PRIVATE -march=x86-64 -mtune=generic)
    elseif(CMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR MATCHES "^(aarch64|arm64|ARM64)$")
      target_compile_options(${target} PRIVATE -march=armv8-a)
    else()
      message(FATAL_ERROR "Declare a CPU floor before adding a portable target")
    endif()
    foundation_link_static_gnu_runtime(${target} PRIVATE)
    # Keep the application's existing protection for every bundled static archive.
    # Installed consumers use the narrower runtime helper to retain their own API.
    target_link_options(${target} PRIVATE "-Wl,--exclude-libs,ALL" "-Wl,--disable-new-dtags")
    set_target_properties(${target} PROPERTIES INSTALL_RPATH "$ORIGIN/../lib/runtime" BUILD_RPATH_USE_ORIGIN ON)
  endif()
  if(FOUNDATION_SANITIZERS)
    if(MSVC OR NOT CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_ID MATCHES "GNU|Clang")
      message(FATAL_ERROR "This sanitizer preset requires GCC or Clang")
    endif()
    target_compile_options(${target} PRIVATE -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-omit-frame-pointer)
    target_link_options(${target} PRIVATE -fsanitize=address,undefined)
  endif()
endfunction()
foundation_options(foundation_core)
if(FOUNDATION_SANITIZERS)
  target_link_options(foundation_core INTERFACE -fsanitize=address,undefined)
endif()

    "${FOUNDATION_SDK_ROOT}" COMMAND_ERROR_IS_FATAL ANY OUTPUT_QUIET)

    foreach(pair "cxx_compiler|CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER" "sysroot|CMAKE_SYSROOT")
      string(REPLACE "|" ";" parts "${pair}")

      if(NOT actual STREQUAL expected)

      endif()

if(BUILD_TESTING)
  add_executable(foundation_core_test EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL tests/store_test.cpp)
  target_link_libraries(foundation_core_test PRIVATE foundation::core)
  foundation_options(foundation_core_test)
  if(NOT EMSCRIPTEN)
  add_test(NAME core.store COMMAND foundation_core_test)
  set_tests_properties(core.store PROPERTIES LABELS "fast;core" TIMEOUT 30)
  add_test(NAME core.cli COMMAND ${Python3_EXECUTABLE}
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/check_cli.py" $<TARGET_FILE:foundation-cli>)
  set_tests_properties(core.cli PROPERTIES LABELS "fast;core" TIMEOUT 30)
  add_test(NAME docs.links COMMAND ${Python3_EXECUTABLE} "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tools/check_docs.py")
  set_tests_properties(docs.links PROPERTIES LABELS "fast;tools" TIMEOUT 30)
  else()
    if(NOT FOUNDATION_NODE_EXECUTABLE OR NOT EXISTS "${FOUNDATION_NODE_EXECUTABLE}")
      message(FATAL_ERROR "Browser tests require the prepared SDK's retained Node executable")
    endif()
    add_test(NAME core.store COMMAND "${FOUNDATION_NODE_EXECUTABLE}" $<TARGET_FILE:foundation_core_test>)
    add_test(NAME core.cli COMMAND ${Python3_EXECUTABLE}
      "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/check_cli.py" "${FOUNDATION_NODE_EXECUTABLE}" $<TARGET_FILE:foundation-cli>)
    set_tests_properties(core.store core.cli PROPERTIES LABELS "fast;core" TIMEOUT 30)
  endif()
  if(WIN32 AND MSVC AND NOT CMAKE_CROSSCOMPILING)
    add_executable(foundation_windows_arguments_test EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL
      tests/cxx_runtime/windows_arguments.cpp)
    target_include_directories(foundation_windows_arguments_test PRIVATE "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src")
    target_compile_features(foundation_windows_arguments_test PRIVATE cxx_std_20)
    foundation_options(foundation_windows_arguments_test)
    add_test(NAME core.windows_arguments COMMAND ${Python3_EXECUTABLE} -B
      "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/cxx_runtime/check_windows_arguments.py"
      $<TARGET_FILE:foundation_windows_arguments_test>)
    set_tests_properties(core.windows_arguments PROPERTIES LABELS "core;fast" TIMEOUT 30)
    foundation_test_prerequisites(core.windows_arguments foundation_windows_arguments_test)
  endif()
  foundation_test_prerequisites(core.store foundation_core_test)
  foundation_test_prerequisites(core.cli foundation-cli)
  add_executable(foundation_rust_component_test EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL tests/rust_component_test.cpp)
  target_link_libraries(foundation_rust_component_test PRIVATE foundation::core)
  target_include_directories(foundation_rust_component_test PRIVATE "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src")
  if(FOUNDATION_CORE_PROVIDER STREQUAL "rust")
    target_compile_definitions(foundation_rust_component_test PRIVATE FOUNDATION_EXPECT_RUST=1)
  endif()
  foundation_options(foundation_rust_component_test)
  if(EMSCRIPTEN)
    add_test(NAME core.text_validation COMMAND "${FOUNDATION_NODE_EXECUTABLE}" $<TARGET_FILE:foundation_rust_component_test>)
  else()
    add_test(NAME core.text_validation COMMAND foundation_rust_component_test)
  endif()
  set_tests_properties(core.text_validation PROPERTIES LABELS "fast;core" TIMEOUT 30)
  foundation_test_prerequisites(core.text_validation foundation_rust_component_test)
  add_executable(foundation_text_status_test EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL tests/rust_component_status_test.cpp src/store.cpp)
  target_include_directories(foundation_text_status_test PRIVATE "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/include" "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src")
  target_compile_features(foundation_text_status_test PRIVATE cxx_std_20)
  foundation_options(foundation_text_status_test)
  if(EMSCRIPTEN)
    add_test(NAME core.text_status COMMAND "${FOUNDATION_NODE_EXECUTABLE}" $<TARGET_FILE:foundation_text_status_test>)
  else()
    add_test(NAME core.text_status COMMAND foundation_text_status_test)
  endif()
  set_tests_properties(core.text_status PROPERTIES LABELS "fast;core" TIMEOUT 30)
  foundation_test_prerequisites(core.text_status foundation_text_status_test)
  if(NOT EMSCRIPTEN)
    foundation_test_prerequisites(docs.links)
  endif()
  # Only explicitly named suites run; adding one requires registering its label.
  set(_tool_suites browser_bundle package_wasm import_wasm ci_retry build build_capacity rev_probe ci_changes package_notices agent_board test_plan artifact gui_boundary gui_source_group gui_visual coverage certification ci_plan qualification_tasks process_tree host_contracts sdk sdk_retention rust_build rust_sdk rust_workflow dependencies source_identity release portability release_check run_tests github_release ci_transport ci_artifacts ci_cleanup ci_cleanup_repository workflow_storage legacy_artifacts verify_legacy_preservation screenshots gallery_browser latest_release windows_graphics windows_compiler)
  set(_platform_exclusions "{}")
  # Docker account IDs, ownership and privilege fixtures apply to Linux hosts.
  if(CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME STREQUAL "Linux")
    list(APPEND _tool_suites container_job prepare_dependencies sdk_paths sdk_build_runtime ci_apt offline_acceptance offline_namespace)
  else()
    foreach(suite container_job prepare_dependencies sdk_paths sdk_build_runtime ci_apt offline_acceptance offline_namespace)
      string(JSON _platform_exclusions SET "${_platform_exclusions}" "tools.${suite}" "\"Linux native dependency and container qualification is not scheduled on this host\"")
    endforeach()
    message(STATUS "Linux Docker ownership qualification is not scheduled on this host")
  endif()
  # Native Windows must use enforced private checkouts until its source-save
  # adapter is separately qualified; skipped POSIX fixtures are not a pass.
  if(UNIX)
    list(APPEND _tool_suites agent_record agent_publish agent_session agent_edit agent_stress agent_migrate)
  else()
    foreach(suite agent_record agent_publish agent_session agent_edit agent_stress agent_migrate)
      string(JSON _platform_exclusions SET "${_platform_exclusions}" "tools.${suite}" "\"POSIX shared source-write qualification is unavailable on this host\"")
    endforeach()
    message(STATUS "Full shared-board source-write qualification is unsupported on this host")
  endif()
  if(FOUNDATION_DISTRIBUTION_TESTS)
    if(NOT CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME STREQUAL "Linux")
      message(FATAL_ERROR "Debian repository tests require Linux")
    endif()
    foreach(_tool dpkg-deb gpg gpgv gpgconf gpg-agent gpg-connect-agent git cc)
      find_program(_required_${_tool} NAMES ${_tool} REQUIRED)
    endforeach()
    list(APPEND _tool_suites apt_repo distro_channel distribution_release distro_client distro_check)
  endif()

    if(NOT EXISTS "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/test_${suite}.py")
      message(FATAL_ERROR "Missing required tool suite: ${suite}")
    endif()
    add_test(NAME tools.${suite} COMMAND ${Python3_EXECUTABLE} "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tools/run_tests.py"
        --suite "${suite}" --output "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/test-reports/${suite}.json")
    foundation_test_prerequisites(tools.${suite})
    set_tests_properties(tools.${suite} PROPERTIES LABELS "tools" TIMEOUT 120)
  endforeach()
  set_tests_properties(tools.gui_boundary tools.gui_source_group tools.gui_visual PROPERTIES LABELS "tools;gui;focused;fast")

files.text:
Software Foundation — command reference

Build and open a desktop window: COMPILE-gui.
Build and open the browser GUI: COMPILE-web.
View or regenerate screenshots: SCREENSHOTS and docs/screenshots.md.

Native prerequisites: Git, CMake >=3.24, Ninja, C++20 compiler, Python >=3.9.
Rust is the default. Debian-family native dev builds additionally use installed
distribution rustc/Cargo (Rust >=1.63) with complete package notices. Release,
ASan, package, portable, Windows, Wasm and prepared-C++-SDK profiles require a
verified --rust-sdk PATH matching that target. Restore inputs before building.
Explicit --core-provider cpp selects the complete legacy build without Rust.
No configuration or normal build downloads or installs software.
Compile concurrency adapts to available CPU/RAM; --build-jobs overrides it.
Test concurrency is independently bounded with --test-jobs.
See docs/development-speed.md for focused checks and delivery scheduling.

./build.sh                                      # incremental Debug build
./build.sh test dev --label core        # smallest core group
./build.sh test dev --label tools       # development-tool contracts
./build.sh test release --rust-sdk /absolute/native-rust-sdk --full
./build.sh test asan --rust-sdk /absolute/native-rust-sdk --full  # C++/boundary instrumentation
./build.sh package release --rust-sdk /absolute/native-rust-sdk # archive; not certification

Windows developer prompt: replace ./build.sh with python tools/build.py and
supply --rust-sdk C:\retained\rust-windows-sdk even for dev.
GUI checkout: ./build.sh test dev --gui --gui-backends terminal,framebuffer,hosted-web --label gui
GUI FLTK: ./build.sh build release --rust-sdk /absolute/native-rust-sdk --gui --gui-backends fltk
GUI inputs: python3 -B gui/source_group.py export --source /absolute/pinned/gui-boundary --output /absolute/gui-input-group
GUI offline: ./build.sh test dev --gui-input-group /absolute/gui-input-group --label gui
GUI source: ./build.sh test dev --gui-source /absolute/pinned/gui-boundary --label gui
SDK: ./build.sh build release --sdk /absolute/prepared-sdk --rust-sdk /absolute/matched-rust-sdk
Wasm: ./build.sh test release --sdk /absolute/wasm-sdk --rust-sdk /absolute/wasm-rust-sdk --gui --gui-backends wasm --label gui
WebAssembly Release retains assertions and exceptions to match the prepared frozen cache.
The same SDK can test core/CLI contracts under retained Node without GUI inputs:
./build.sh test release --sdk /absolute/wasm-sdk --rust-sdk /absolute/wasm-rust-sdk --gui-backends wasm --label core --build-dir build/wasm-core
Native GUI and Wasm GUI use separate build/dev-rust-gui and build/release-sdk-rust-sdk-gui trees.
Core-only Wasm uses build/release-sdk-rust-sdk. SDKs and complete recovery groups remain
outside Git; normal app iterations reuse them without rebuilding dependencies.
Retain Windows host tools and the Microsoft offline installer layout as well;
see docs/sdk.md. Rev needs a newer toolchain than stock Bookworm.

Direct CMake (also supports generators other than Ninja):
cmake --preset dev -DFOUNDATION_RUST_SDK_ROOT=/absolute/native-rust-sdk
cmake --build build/dev --target foundation-tests --parallel "$(python3 tools/build_capacity.py)"
ctest --test-dir build/dev --output-on-failure --no-tests=error --parallel 2
cmake --install build/dev --prefix /absolute/staging-prefix

Visual Studio and Ninja Multi-Config require --config Release for build/install,
-C Release for CTest and -C Release for CPack. See docs/building.md.
Do not run tests from a stale build tree or assume CTest compiles prerequisites.
See docs/testing.md, docs/sdk.md and docs/portability.md for scope and prerequisites.
Default policy rationale: docs/rust-hybrid-plan.md#why-rust-is-the-default.

Software Foundation — build and open a desktop window

Run from the repository root on a Linux desktop with a working display.
Requires Git, CMake >=3.24, Ninja, a C++20 compiler, Python >=3.9, and
the FLTK development package with its platform dependencies. Rust is the default:
these Debian-family native dev examples use installed distribution rustc/Cargo.
Other native hosts need --rust-sdk /absolute/matched-rust-sdk.
Debian 12 preparation, if needed:
sudo apt-get install git build-essential cmake ninja-build python3 rustc cargo libfltk1.3-dev

Build and launch the FLTK application:
./build.sh build dev --gui --gui-backends fltk --build-dir build/demo-fltk
./build/demo-fltk/gui/foundation-gui-fltk

An "Entry list" window opens. Type text in "New entry", select "Add entry",
then try "Count text". Close the window to exit. Entries are held in memory;
use Actions -> Export entries to save them before closing.
Rerun the same build command after source changes, then launch again.

SDL window alternative (also requires the SDL2 development package):
./build.sh build dev --gui --gui-backends sdl --build-dir build/demo-sdl
./build/demo-sdl/gui/foundation-gui-sdl

These commands use the GUI sources retained in this checkout. Ordinary builds
do not download dependencies. Debian-family dev can use installed Rust packages;
release and qualified target profiles need their retained Rust extension. Each backend recipe
has its own build directory; use a fresh directory when changing toolchain or
backend selection. Compile concurrency is automatic; --build-jobs overrides it.

Browser GUI without a native toolkit: see COMPILE-web.
Screenshots of all seven hosts: see docs/screenshots.md and SCREENSHOTS.
Terminal, framebuffer image, Rev and platform details:
docs/gui-boundary.md#build-and-run and #prepared-platform-dependencies.
Windows: initialize the compiler and matching toolkit dependencies described
there, replace ./build.sh with python tools/build.py, and add .exe to the
executable name and --rust-sdk C:\retained\rust-windows-sdk to each build command.
These recipes use the wrapper's single-configuration Ninja.
Build reference: docs/building.md. Focused checks: docs/testing.md.

Software Foundation — build and open the browser GUI

Run from the repository root. Requires Git, CMake >=3.24, Ninja, a C++20
compiler, Python >=3.9, and a current browser. No native GUI toolkit or
prepared C++ SDK is needed for the hosted-browser example. Rust is the default;
Debian-family dev requires installed distribution rustc/Cargo, while another
native host needs --rust-sdk /absolute/matched-rust-sdk.

Build and start the hosted application:
./build.sh build dev --gui --gui-backends hosted-web --build-dir build/demo-web
python3 -B build/demo-web/gui/web/serve.py --executable build/demo-web/gui/foundation-gui-web

Open the loopback URL printed by the server in your browser. Keep its terminal
running. The page shows "Entry list": type text, select "Add entry", then try
"Count text". Each tab owns a separate in-memory collection. Use Actions ->
Export entries and the browser's Download button to save entries.
Press Ctrl+C in the server terminal to stop the server and its sessions.
The server uses an already-built executable; rerun the build command after
source changes, then restart the server and reload the page.

The GUI sources are retained in this checkout; normal builds download nothing.
Keep build/demo-web separate from native-toolkit and Wasm trees. A changed
toolchain or backend selection needs a fresh build directory.
On Windows, initialize a developer prompt, use python tools/build.py instead
of ./build.sh and python instead of python3, append .exe to the executable, and
add --rust-sdk C:\retained\rust-windows-sdk to the build command.

Optional self-contained Wasm application (Linux x86_64 host):
This route needs the separate matched browser and Rust SDK extensions; the Windows substitution
above applies to the hosted-native recipe, not this SDK.
Replace both paths with verified Emscripten 6.0.10/Rust 1.63 inputs in docs/sdk.md.
./build.sh build release --gui --gui-backends wasm --sdk /absolute/prepared-wasm-sdk --rust-sdk /absolute/prepared-wasm-rust-sdk --build-dir build/demo-wasm

Open build/demo-wasm/gui/wasm-package/software-foundation-wasm.html in a browser.
That single file contains the application and runs without a server or network.
Preparing the SDK is a separate operation; the command never downloads one.

Native window: COMPILE-gui. Screenshots: docs/screenshots.md and SCREENSHOTS.
Transport, session and platform details: docs/gui-boundary.md#build-and-run.
Offline Wasm package: docs/gui-boundary.md#worker-execution-and-an-offline-browser-application.
Build reference: docs/building.md. Focused checks: docs/testing.md.

Not implemented
===============

Optional improvements for later work; these are not pending qualification or
authorization to execute. Reuse existing mechanisms and preserve their safeguards.

- Publication-only reuse of qualified CI artifacts, binding original consumer
  evidence and exact bytes without rebuilding or relaying through a workstation.
- Authenticated assembly/retry reuse of successful producers with unchanged inputs,
  preserving original attempts and complete required inventories.
- Earlier native platform diagnostics for affected contracts before costly dependent
  builds, while retaining required final qualification.
- Compact evidence reporting that distinguishes execution, retention, qualification
  and publication and links the original receipts.
- Conservative development-check selection if measurements justify it, retaining
  broad coverage for unknown dependencies and shared build changes.
- Thin agent-operation wrappers if necessary to remove repeated bookkeeping while
  preserving ownership checks, supervised completion and failure handling.


Test parallelism follow-ups (separate discussion)
-----------------------------------------------

- Replace fixed two/four-worker test defaults with CPU- and RAM-aware concurrency,
  reusing tools/build_capacity.py and the existing test planners. Respect CPU
  affinity/container limits, explicit operator overrides and shared-resource locks.
  Coordinate nested build/test workers so each child does not independently claim
  the whole machine. Preserve complete coverage and operation on standard runners.

- Parallelize the slow Python suites with isolated worker processes, using existing
  timing receipts to select useful partitions rather than spawning a process for
  every small test. Extend tools/run_tests.py and the existing inventory/aggregation
  mechanisms while preserving module/class fixture semantics, per-case results and
  explicit platform exclusions. Reject missing, duplicate, skipped or failed cases;
  retain bounded execution, descendant cleanup and complete diagnostic evidence.

- Run independent backend checks concurrently within certification batches.
  Extend the existing check_batch/prepared_checks machinery: Linux already creates
  a fresh container per case, but batch execution is sequential. Reuse verified
  inputs and prepared images while giving concurrent checks separate writable
  workspaces, evidence directories, temporary resources and owned displays. Handle
  native Windows shared resources explicitly. Preserve source/recovery separation,
  every backend receipt, failure aggregation and cleanup before evidence publication.
  Keep operations with real ordering or host-wide state requirements, such as
  package upgrades and firewall changes, ordered or isolated on separate hosts.

# Software Foundation A generic reference repository for developing, testing, maintaining and delivering software. The application is deliberately domain-neutral: an owning, bounded record collection, a command-line application, and an optional shared GUI application. The engineering mechanisms are comprehensive: application size does not reduce coordination, supply, recovery or qualification requirements. C++20 and CMake make the build and binary compatibility examples concrete; the ownership, testing, documentation and delivery rules apply across languages. The default build combines C++ with a Rust component implementing the private text-validation contract shared by the CLI and every GUI frontend. This makes the reviewed Rust boundary the normal starting point for further application logic; the present application remains predominantly C++. ## One application, seven backends Each host presents the same shared **Entry list** application. The six graphical captures show the 2026-10-02 source snapshot; the TUI uses the corrected 2026-10-04 local capture. Select an image to view it at full size. | FLTK native window | Rev native window | | --- | --- | | [](docs/screenshots/fltk.png) | [](docs/screenshots/rev.png) | | **SDL window** | **Framebuffer** | | [](docs/screenshots/sdl.png) | [](docs/screenshots/framebuffer.png) | | **Hosted browser** | **Browser Wasm** | | [](docs/screenshots/hosted-web.png) | [](docs/screenshots/wasm.png) | **Terminal UI** [](docs/terminal-caret/terminal.png) [Capture details and provenance](docs/screenshots.md#view-screenshots) identify the exact source and image bytes. [SCREENSHOTS](SCREENSHOTS) points to the capture job and refresh instructions. All images are included in the checkout. Start with the [engineering contract](docs/engineering-contract.md), [requirements and practice map](docs/requirements.md), [repository map](docs/architecture.md), and [documentation index](docs/README.md). Missing Rust inputs fail clearly; normal operations acquire no tools or crates. `--core-provider cpp` explicitly selects the complete legacy build, which performs no Rust discovery. [The default-policy rationale](docs/rust-hybrid-plan.md#why-rust-is-the-default) explains the security and maintenance choice and its limits. [Platform limits](docs/portability.md#rust-provider-boundary) and [the implementation record](docs/rust-hybrid-plan.md) separate working code from observed qualification. ## Run the GUI On a Linux desktop, install the native build prerequisites above plus the FLTK development package (`libfltk1.3-dev` on Debian 12). From the repository root, build and open the application: ```sh ./build.sh build dev --gui --gui-backends fltk --build-dir build/demo-fltk ./build/demo-fltk/gui/foundation-gui-fltk ``` The **Entry list** window starts empty. Type text in **New entry**, select **Add entry**, then try **Count text**. Close the window to exit. Entries are held in memory; **Actions → Export entries** saves them to a file. [COMPILE-gui](COMPILE-gui) includes prerequisites and an SDL alternative. Each recipe uses a separate build directory and the GUI sources already retained in this checkout. ## What is executable here | Area | Included example | Qualification boundary | | --- | --- | --- | | Application | Library, CLI, validation, owned data, stable IDs | Bounded in-memory record contract with explicit failure guarantees | | Build | One CMake graph, presets, wrapper, focused prerequisite targets | One build tree per configuration and toolchain | | Tests | Contract checks, tool regressions, installed consumer, disjoint shards | Full means all tests enabled in that configuration | | GUI | All seven hosts consume one application widget-definition table;
